ai.literal: The family called undiminishing lamp, [when] the dirt called laziness spreads, having been extinguished will perish.
ai.translation: The unfailing lamp of one's family will be extinguished and destroyed when the soot of laziness spreads over it.
ai.modern: குடி என்னும் அணையாத விளக்கு, மடி என்னும் மாசு படிந்தால் அணைந்து அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses the metaphor of a lamp to describe a family's reputation and prosperity. The family is called an 'undiminishing lamp' that shines brightly across generations. Laziness is compared to 'dirt' (மாசு), which in the context of a lamp specifically means the soot that creeps over it. When the soot of laziness spreads, it blocks the light and eventually extinguishes the flame, causing the family's greatness to perish. The imagery clearly warns that sloth destroys a household's enduring legacy.

ai.literal: Laziness as destruction conducting oneself, family as family those who desire.
ai.translation: Those who desire their family to be a true family must conduct themselves by treating laziness as destruction.
ai.modern: தம் குடியைச் சிறந்த குடியாக உயர்த்த விரும்புபவர், சோம்பலைத் தமக்கு அழிவு என்று கருதி அதனை விலக்கி வாழ வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a clever play on the word 'maṭi', which means both 'laziness' and 'destruction'. It creates a parallel structure: just as one desires their family ('kuṭi') to be a true family ('kuṭiyāka'), they must treat laziness ('maṭiyai') as destruction ('maṭiyā'). The message is that anyone wishing to elevate their lineage must conduct themselves with the constant awareness that sluggishness will ruin their efforts.

ai.literal: Laziness having taken into the lap behaving fool born family will perish than himself before.
ai.translation: The family of a fool who lives embracing laziness in his lap will perish even before he does.
ai.modern: சோம்பலைத் தன் மடியில் கட்டிக்கொண்டு வாழும் அறிவிலி பிறந்த குடியானது, அவன் அழிவதற்கு முன்பாகவே அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the destructive power of laziness on one's entire lineage. The poet brilliantly uses the word 'மடி' (maṭi) in three different senses: first as 'laziness', second as 'lap' (embracing laziness in one's lap), and third as 'to perish'. It means that if a foolish person harbors laziness as a cherished possession, his family's reputation and prosperity will die out even before his own physical death.

ai.literal: Family having perished fault will increase, laziness having yielded to, excellent effort to those without.
ai.translation: For those who yield to laziness and lack excellent effort, their family will perish and their faults will multiply.
ai.modern: சோம்பலில் வீழ்ந்து சிறந்த முயற்சி இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு, அவர்களின் குடி அழிந்து குற்றங்கள் பெருகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the destructive consequences of laziness on one's lineage and character. The word 'மடி' means laziness, and yielding to it prevents a person from making the excellent effort needed to succeed. Consequently, their family's standing is destroyed and their personal flaws and failures multiply.

ai.literal: Delay, forgetfulness, laziness, sleep - all four [are] the desired vessel of those of ruinous nature.
ai.translation: Procrastination, forgetfulness, laziness, and excessive sleep—these four are the chosen vessels of those destined for ruin.
ai.modern: காலம் தாழ்த்துதல், மறதி, சோம்பல், தூக்கம் ஆகிய இந்த நான்கும், அழியும் இயல்புடையவர்கள் விரும்பி ஏறும் கப்பல் ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet lists four negative traits: procrastination, forgetfulness, laziness, and excessive sleep. It describes these four as the desired vessel or boat (காமக் கலன்) for people whose nature leads them to ruin (கெடுநீரார்). Just as a traveler chooses a boat to reach a destination, those heading toward destruction willingly embrace these four habits. By recognizing and avoiding these traits, one can escape the path to failure.

ai.literal: Earth possessors' support secured even when, laziness possessors excellent benefit attaining is difficult.
ai.translation: Even if they secure the support of kings who rule the earth, it is difficult for the lazy to attain any glorious benefits.
ai.modern: உலகத்தை ஆளும் அரசர்களின் ஆதரவு கிடைத்தாலும், சோம்பல் உடையவர்கள் சிறந்த பயன்களை அடைவது கடினம்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that external advantages cannot compensate for internal flaws like laziness. The word 'paṭi' means the earth, and 'paṭiyuṭaiyār' refers to kings or powerful rulers who possess it. Even if a person secures the strong support ('paṟṟu') of such powerful figures, their own laziness ('maṭi') will prevent them from achieving any excellent results ('māṇ payan'). True success requires personal effort, regardless of how much backing one has.

ai.literal: Reproof having made, mocking word they will hear; laziness having desired, excellent effort those without.
ai.translation: Those who embrace laziness and lack excellent effort will hear words of harsh reproof and mockery.
ai.modern: சோம்பலை விரும்பிச் சிறந்த முயற்சி இல்லாதவர்கள், பிறர் இடித்துரைத்து இகழும் சொற்களைக் கேட்பார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the social consequences of laziness. The word 'maṭi' means laziness or sloth, while 'uñatṟu' refers to exertion or effort. Those who choose laziness over excellent effort will inevitably face harsh criticism. The phrase 'iṭi purintu' evokes the image of striking reproof, showing that their lack of effort will draw severe and mocking words from others.

ai.literal: Laziness in noble birth if it stays, to one's own foes slavery having caused to enter it will leave.
ai.translation: If laziness takes root in a person of noble birth, it will force them into slavery under their own enemies.
ai.modern: ஒரு நல்ல குடியில் பிறந்தவனிடம் சோம்பல் தங்கிவிட்டால், அது அவனை அவனுடைய பகைவர்களுக்கு அடிமையாக்கி விடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the severe consequences of laziness for someone born into a good family. The word 'குடிமை' refers to noble birth or family honor, which requires active effort to maintain. If sluggishness ('மடிமை') is allowed to stay ('தங்கின்'), it strips away this independence and strength. Ultimately, it reduces the person to a state of servitude ('அடிமை') to their very enemies, contrasting the dignity of a noble lineage with the humiliation of slavery.

If a person simply removes their laziness, those faults will automatically perish, restoring the family's strength.

ai.literal: Laziness-without king will-attain foot-he-who-measured spanned-that all together.
ai.translation: A king who is free from laziness will attain all at once the entire world spanned by the one who measured it with his foot.
ai.modern: சோம்பல் இல்லாத அரசன், தன் அடியால் உலகத்தை அளந்தவன் கடந்த நிலப்பரப்பு முழுவதையும் ஒருசேர அடைவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the boundless rewards of being free from laziness. It uses the image of the one who measured the universe with his steps to represent the entirety of the world. A ruler who is completely devoid of idleness will effortlessly and entirely attain such a vast dominion. The word 'ஒருங்கு' (together or at once) highlights that this immense success comes completely and comprehensively to the tireless leader.
